chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The one who prevents a Right of Allah (Mighty and Majestic) would spend double the like of it in falsehood (the wrong way).
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of withholding Zakat or Khums according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the spiritual consequence of withholding divine rights, specifically linking the act of retention to the squandering of wealth in vain. Scholars interpret 'double' as either a literal multiplication of loss or a metaphorical emphasis on the disproportionate cost of neglecting one's duty to Allah. This principle underscores the economic wisdom of Zakat and Khums as purifying mechanisms that prevent the erosion of wealth through mismanagement or divine displeasure.
